source.citation: Lu Y, Xiao K, Pointer M, et al. The International Skin Spectra Archive (ISSA): a multicultural human skin phenotype and colour spectra collection. Sci Data 2025;12:487. doi:10.1038/s41597-025-04857-5

space: linear sRGB albedo under D65, CIE 1931 2 degree observer (the reduction of the face's skin-albedo norms, whose cheek means it reproduces)
method: each subject's repeated measurements at a site averaged, then averaged per ancestry group and sex; for each site, the group-and-sex means with at least five subjects measured at that site are paired with the same group's cheek mean (site code 2), and per channel a least-squares line is fitted in logarithms, ln site = a + b * ln cheek, so albedo = exp(a) * cheek^b. Pigment absorbs multiplicatively, so the site follows the cheek as a power. The fit is made across group means rather than across individuals because one cheek reading measures a person's pigmentation with noise, and the individual-level fit regresses toward the archive's mean: pooled over subjects it overpredicted the darkest group's inner arm by 30 to 36% in green and blue, where the group-mean fit is within 7%.
individualLevel: the same pairs fitted over individual subjects (776 to 1,711 per site) give R^2 0.46 to 0.85 per channel, the share of a site's variance across people that one cheek reading explains
assignment: the trunk, thighs and other covered skin take the protected inner arm (the archive measures no trunk or leg site); forearms the exposed outer arm; shanks and the backs of the feet half of each; the palm and the sole the palm; the back of the hand its own; the neck and head bones the neck; a band of 4 cm below the neck's cut blends from the cheek, which the face wears, to the sites
